entries.reason: CMTagCollection arrived at iOS 17 and CMTaggedBufferGroup with it, and the SDK the toolchain resolves is 16.4, where none of CMTag, CMTagCollection or CMTaggedBufferGroup exists at all. CharonCMTag26.h transcribes 26.2's declarations for the tag collection and that half is carried; this type is not written, because nothing about the host's answers for it has been measured and a shape guessed from the header is what the brief forbids (facts/CoreMedia/TagCollection.md, the CMTaggedBufferGroup section)

entries.effect: a format description for the group, made with CMFormatDescriptionCreate at media type video and media subtype 'tbgr' - measured 1952606066, and its CFTypeID is CMFormatDescriptionGetTypeID()'s, so a caller gets the platform's own type - carrying the group's per-entry tag collections in its extensions dictionary as CFData, a CMItemCount and that collection's tags per entry in order. A NULL group is not a failure: the host answers 0 and hands back a real description matching nothing, and the reason is visible - there are no entries to record

entries.effect: true when the group's per-entry tag collections equal the description's, in order and by content, and nothing else. Three cases fix that: the group it came from is 1; a group of the same tags over different buffers is 1, so buffers are not part of it; a group of the same entry SIZES over different tags is 0, so it is not a count; two entries is 0 and NULL is 0. The comparison is the port's own tag equality over each collection's sorted storage, because CFEqual has nothing to say about a bridged Objective-C class
